speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling
text: asked the Minister for Health (a) when will the national digital health app HealthHub extend its current function of appointments management across all three public healthcare clusters to include Healthier SG general practitioner (GP) clinics; and (b) whether the rest of the current functions on HealthHub, such as laboratory report, medical refill, health screening and CHAS balance, can be extended to these GP clinics.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng
text: asked the Minister for Health (a) whether the Ministry has studied public feedback requesting for a single fully consolidated public sector app for patients to transact with the public healthcare clusters; and (b) whether there is room for improvement in existing platforms, especially for patients receiving care across multiple healthcare clusters.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary) (for the Minister for Health)
text: My response will also cover the matters raised in the question by Ms Ng Ling Ling1 which is scheduled for a subsequent Sitting.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: I invite Ms Ng to seek clarifications, if need be.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: If the question has been addressed, it may not be necessary for the Member to proceed with the Question for a future Sitting.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: One of its key functions is appointment booking.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: At this stage, we do not think it is appropriate to compel all private GPs to come onto the app.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: They are private clinics and they are operating within a market, albeit one that is heavily regulated.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: We have not received much feedback on the difficulties in making cross-cluster medical appointments.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: This may be because the public are also familiar with alternative booking channels, such as the call centres of the institutions.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: From time to time, we will receive suggestions to consolidate the cluster apps under HealthHub.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: The cluster apps do serve a purpose, in having features customised to their particular facilities and services.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: These apps also allow the clusters to innovate on user-interaction features, helping them to better connect with and address the unique needs of the patients they serve.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: On the other hand, there are also advantages to having a consolidated HealthHub.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: This is an issue that we will continue to explore.

speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
text: It is through that link that you can go in and make appointments with the GP clinic that you have enrolled with under Healthier SG, instead of the normal quick link to "Appointments" that most patients would have used HealthHub to make appointments.

speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
text: My first question is: can the Ministry of Health (MOH) consider using the quick link "Appointment" button that a lot of people are very familiar with if they had been using HealthHub to also make appointments with GP clinics that Singaporeans had enrolled with under Healthier SG?

speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
text: My second question is: I think I have a very good GP who goes over and above the extra mile, even when his clinic is very crowded, to explain to me when I ask questions.

speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
text: That took him an extra two to three minutes.

speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
text: I think some of these other GPs are really doing a good job trying to support Healthier SG which MOH is promoting.

speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Will MOH recognise and give some award to encourage these GPs and encourage what we want to see other GPs doing, as we extend Healthier SG in the coming years?

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: We will consider both and look at them closely.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: Indeed, we are always looking to see how we can improve the user interface and user experience of our digital products.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: I am glad that she has found a GP that she trusts and is providing her with quality, in-depth care.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: I think we do need to find ways to reognise and incentivise this type of behaviour from the family physicians that look after all of us.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
text: Can I ask the Senior Minister of State what lessons can we learn from drawing on GovTech's experience to improve the user experience of MOH's apps and the healthcare cluster apps?

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
text: For example, GovTech has a deep pool of capable staff, some who have even got experience at major international tech firms such as Google.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
text: Because I have residents who tell me that apps such as LifeSG and in particular, Parking.sg, are much, much easier to use than the hospital clusters apps, or even HealthHub.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
text: So, can I ask the Senior Minister of State along those lines further?

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
text: Is there a lot of user interface testing done for HealthHub and the hospital apps, and is that user interface testing applied to populations, including the elderly and people who may not be naturally tech savvy?

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: And currently, that may mean navigating different apps to manage medical transactions across institutions for themselves and their family members.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: So, we are looking at ways and how we can improve our digital services.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: We are indeed learning from the experience across the rest of the digitalisation in the public sector that GovTech and others have been heavily involved in.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: The teams that are working with the healthcare service providers – we have the Synapxe digital team, we also have got the GovTech teams, as well as private vendors.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: So, there is a significant amount of experience from the public sector and the private sector, drawing on the lessons of other care and business process transformation and applying that to what happens within the healthcare ecosystem.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: Dr Tan made a point about the consolidation of the apps and the user interface.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: These are, in a way, two distinct issues.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: I take his feedback and we will continue to try our best.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: And if there are specific suggestions about buttons, banners, transactions, workflows, I would encourage him and other Members to provide us the information and we will certainly find a way to optimise the experience for all our users.
